blindSummary:
This territory is an overseas part integral to a distant metropolitan state: metropolitan law applies fully and directly (marriage equality, anti-discrimination protections, legal gender recognition).

Relative to the metropolitan country, local risk is elevated: weaker local institutions, higher general crime, and a more socially conservative local climate.
blindOutOfScope: An overseas part of the metropolitan state; local deviations noted in the summary.
blindSourceSummaries: News outlet feature (Jan 2018, metropolitan context): trans women incarcerated in the metropolitan state on the basis of their legal gender fall into a legal gray area - directly relevant to this territory, which applies the same metropolitan law.

The metropolitan state's places-of-detention watchdog, opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty (metropolitan framework, applicable in this territory): serious violations persist across places of detention.

An online encyclopaedia page on transgender rights in this territory: the metropolitan state's national framework applies - simplified legal gender recognition since 2017 (administrative declaration, no surgery/sterilisation/diagnosis required), anti-discrimination protections since 2012, hate-crime provisions since 2017; but specialist trans healthcare is limited by remoteness; societal transphobia and cultural taboos discourage visibility and reporting.
